newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO CETES RATE EDGES UP ON AUCTION RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO CETES RATE EDGES UP ON AUCTION RESULTS.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 45 basis points at 18.75 percent in mid-morning trade on Wednesday.
Dealers said secondary rates had edged higher in the wake of increased primary rates at the central bank auction the night before.

Wednesday saw the cutoff for banks to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank. Traders said most banks now had sufficient liquidity to meet the dealine and did not expect a reptition of turbulence seen in recent sessions.
Overnight rates on bank paper declined by 35 basis points to 19.50 percent.
Liquidity of 711 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system during the session from prior central bank participation.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended down 110 basis points at 18.75 percent.
Banco de Mexico drained 2.736 billion pesos from the market by placing three direct Cetes sales and five repos.
